newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Merck surprises with upbeat figures.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Merck surprises with upbeat figures.

text.p: German pharmaceutical group Merck KGaA surprised the market on Wednesday as nine-month profit and sales figures rose beyond expectations, with its activities in the Americas the engine for growth.
Profit from ordinary activities in the first nine months of the year rose 25 percent to 577 million marks ($384.3 million) on turnover up nearly 10 percent at 5.16 billion marks.

Merck said it expects to report clearly higher earnings for full-year 1996, but declined to be more specific on actual earnings. It said above-average growth in the pharmaceuticals sector meant the prospects for 1997 were encouraging.

Merck cited the good performance of its north American business as a major factor in its nine-month figures, where strong demand for pharmaceuticals helped turnover in the period to increase 18 percent.
Sales gains in Europe and Asia were more modest, both rising some seven percent.

Management board chairman Hans Joachim Langmann said at a news conference in Darmstadt to announce the group's nine-month figures: "It is beyond question that we will again report increased earnings in full-year 1996."
"Even if we just added one third of what we've earned already this year that would (represent) growth of around 30 percent," said Langmann.
However, he went on to say the figure could be more or could be less.

Langmann did not want to give a precise earnings forecast, especially in the crucial end-of-year phase. While sales and gross profit had grown in October, an overrun in the state's prescription budget had hit the pharmaceutical sector.
This would continue in December and for next year.

The German stock market responded positively to the figures and the outlook for the company, and Merck closed bourse trade on the German DAX-30 index of blue-chips at 56.75 marks, up two marks or nearly three percent.
Analysts were cautiously upbeat on the company.

Christiane Dienhart, chemicals analyst at Bayerische Vereinsbank in Munich, said: "I would say we are carefully positive on Merck. The figures are a little better than I expected, but I still want some clarification on income from participations."
Vereinsbank has earnings per share (EPS) forecasts for 1996 and 1997 of 2.40 marks and 2.80 marks respectively.

"If I discover after the analysts' conference call today that these figures are usable then I can raise the EPS outlook by around 10 pfennigs. I was expecting to be positively surprised," said Dienhart.
Martin Wirth, chemicals analyst at Bank Julius Baer in Frankfurt, was also positive.
"The third quarter figures were better than the half-year figures, and the growth rates seem better than in the previous year, although the previous year wasn't great," said Wirth.

Markus Rausch, chemicals analyst at DB Research in Frankfurt, said: "I had a relatively aggressive earnings outlook anyway, so the figures were in line with my expectations. I think a lot of the optimism is discounted in the share price."
